english.title: Aid and abet fraud by abuse of position
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) **(..SPECIFY DETAILS OF OFFENCE..)
english.legislation: Contrary to sections 1 and 4 of the Fraud Act 2006.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
aided /abetted / counselled / procured a person
occupying a position in which he /she was expected
to safeguard / not to act against the financial interests of another
dishonestly abused that position
intending to make a gain for him / herself / another OR
intending to cause loss to another / expose another to a risk of loss

english.notes:
See H8687 and H9067 respectively for the substantive and " attempt " variation of this offence.

(i) Section 4(2) of the Fraud Act 2006 provides that a person may be regarded as having abused his position even though his conduct consisted of an omission rather than an act. There is no definition for the term abuse; it is intended to cover a wide range of conduct.
(ii) The test for dishonesty in all criminal cases is that established in the case of Ivey v Genting Casinos (UK) Ltd (trading as Crockfords) 2017, as confirmed in R v Barton and another (2020).
(iii) The offence requires an intention of making a gain or causing loss or risk of loss; the gain or loss does not actually have to take place.
(iv) The offence applies to situations where a person is in a privileged position, and by virtue of this position is expected to safeguard another's financial interests or not to act against them. The necessary relationship will be present between trustee and beneficiary, director and company, professional person and client, agent and principal, employee and employer, or between partners, but could also arise within a family or in the context of voluntary work.
(v) Fraud can also be committed by false representation, section 2 of the Act and H8685, and by failing to disclose information, section 3 of the Act and H8686.
(vi) Section 12 of the Act makes provision for directors, managers, secretaries or other similar officers or person purporting to act in such a capacity to be liable to prosecution where a body corporate has committed this offence.

other.penalty:
Either way -
Summary: maximum 6 / 12 months imprisonment and/or fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
Indictment: maximum 10 years imprisonment and/or fine.

The maximum penalty on summary conviction is 6 months for offences committed before 2nd May 2022; for offences committed on or after that date it may be 6 or 12 months depending on the general limit in a magistrates’ court, see section 1(3) of the Fraud Act 2006 and section 224(1) and (1A) of the Sentencing Act 2020.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
